• Ask for the carrier's reasons in writing; a named reason can be answered, a vague one cannot
• Four elements every suit proves: duty, breach, causation, damages, each backed by a checked exhibit

theory.say:
• Two neutrals: Hon. Carla Benton (Ret.) helps parties agree; Laura Whitcomb, Esq. decides, with almost no appeal
• Judge Benton, the mediator, can't decide anything; brackets, ranges and authority belong to Atty. Thorne and John
• Pre-suit: mediation usually follows treatment and the demand; arbitration only where a signed clause forces it
• After filing, courts often order mediation during discovery, when both sides swap evidence; both of John Doe's sessions sit on the filed side
• Non-binding (mediation): both sides must agree; nobody is forced to settle
• Binding (arbitration): the award is final, enforced like a court order, reviewed only on narrow grounds; meaning for John is Atty. Thorne's to explain

frame.say:
• Role: the mediator facilitates and negotiates; the arbitrator is a private judge and finder of fact
• Decision power: mediator none; arbitrator issues a binding Arbitration Award
• Outcome: parties control it at mediation; the arbitrator decides liability and damages and can exclude evidence
• Review: none needed for mediation; narrow court review for arbitration
• Common mistake: preparing for both the same way; compromise focus versus trial-ready
• In the room: joint session if the mediator sets one; private caucus; shuttle moves, each logged; brackets only from counsel; term sheet in writing 03/18/2027

why.say:

• Bottleneck: anything stuck and holding the rest of the file up
• They look like a quiet inbox, a record "on its way", a date nobody confirmed

theory.say:
• Two families of bottlenecks
• Compromise traps stall a mediation: an unverified ledger (unchecked bill list), a representative without authority to pay, a late brief
• Trial-ready landmines can sink a binding arbitration: excluded exhibits, unprotected prior records, missed cutoffs
• Prior medical shield: answering old records, said to show wear and tear, with records and a doctor's opinion
• Two habits clear most early: the 48-hour audit, checking every lien against insurance payment statements

frame.say:
• Six common bottlenecks, three per forum
• Mediation: unverified ledger, missing decision-maker without real settlement authority, late confidential brief missing critical exhibits
• Arbitration: evidence exclusion from missing documents or black-and-white prints
• Also the pre-existing defense trap, old injury records with no doctor's answer, and calendar misses
• The unverified ledger costs most; an unscanned record doesn't exist yet

rules.say:
• Bottleneck: anything that can stop the file reaching a hard date; log it the day it starts, with its threatened date
• Follow up a silent adjuster every 5 business days: Keystone left 08/24 and 08/31/2026 unanswered, then 09/02 escalation
• Record silence as dated facts: what, since when, what date at risk; never "adjuster busy"
• Record unanswered 14 days is a bottleneck; ledger $42,984.00, Riverton $6,105.00, Peach State $1,860.00
• Brief to Hon. Carla Benton by 03/11/2027; chase, document, flag; remedies and value are Atty. Thorne's

• Biggest card: non-responsive party, red callout "$10,000 carrier, $40,000 frozen"
• Right edge: at mediation a gap costs leverage; at arbitration it costs evidence
• Measure a bottleneck by the hard date it threatens

dodont.say:

• A gap before mediation costs leverage; before arbitration it can get evidence excluded
• Strong entry: a call, an email, a date for each, the next follow-up calendared

theory.say:

• Send a decision-ready report the reader can act on in one read

frame.say:

• Level three, legal: Atty. Thorne's motion to compel (court order to hand over), subpoena or LOP, his choice
• Step two is the one most often skipped
